DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING MARKUP OF H.R. 7661
Committee Democrats put forward five amendments to improve the bill. These amendments would have ensured that the bill did not unfairly target trans and LGBTQ youth, include the teaching of diverse cultures, religions, and communities as allowable content for children and ensure that teaching children how to protect themselves from grooming and sex trafficking is allowed. Committee Republicans rejected four of the five Democratic amendments that were considered.

CONCLUSION
This Committee should be laser focused on issues that would help improving academic achievement, addressing concerns around student mental health, strengthening the educator pipeline, and the harrowing effect of efforts to dismantle the Department of Education. Instead, H.R. 7661 attempts to circumvent longstanding prohibitions on federal control over locally controlled aspects of education. It does so by forcing local states and districts to adopt a partisan, divisive viewpoint. If they do not, they may be prohibited from using funds Congress authorized to support our most vulnerable students through the ESEA.\24\ For the reasons stated above, all Committee Democrats present opposed H.R. 7661 when the Committee on Education and the Workforce considered it on March 17, 2026. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
